Used in the destination topic name (DefaultReplicationPolicy names it alias, separator, topic).
The pipeline reads the source cluster.

Kafka Connect's producer writes the records to the worker's cluster; this fills the destination's servers when neither the worker file nor producer.override.bootstrap.servers sets them, and MirrorMaker requires the two to be the same cluster.
SASL_PLAINTEXT sends the SASL credentials without TLS. The Kafka connector (v0.15.0 and later) refuses SASL without TLS, and the migration never writes a plaintext SASL setup by itself.
entries.fix: Enable TLS on the cluster and use SASL_SSL, or set saslAllowPlaintext true (with tls.enabled false) on the migrated pipeline by hand, knowing that it exposes the SASL credentials on the network.

entries.reason: The username is written to saslUsername; saslPassword is ${KC_MM2_MSC_PLAINTEXT_SOURCE_CLUSTER_SASL_JAAS_CONFIG}, to be filled with the password from this JAAS config.
The username is written to saslUsername; saslPassword is ${KC_MM2_MSC_PLAINTEXT_TARGET_CLUSTER_SASL_JAAS_CONFIG}, to be filled with the password from this JAAS config.

notes.reason: Records keep their key, value and topic name (per the replication policy), but not their partition, headers or timestamp. This version does not write the Kafka mirror settings; the destination partitions by key and stamps the time of writing.
notes.fix: Keep this flow on MirrorMaker if consumers rely on partition numbers, headers or record timestamps, or accept the difference with --accept-gaps.

notes.reason: MirrorMaker resumes every partition from the offsets Kafka Connect stored for it, and reads a partition with none from the beginning unless auto.offset.reset says otherwise. migrate does not carry the stored offsets over. The pipeline reads every partition from the beginning (readFromBeginning: true), so the records MirrorMaker already copied are copied again.
notes.fix: Stop the MirrorMaker connector before starting the pipeline, and accept the re-copied or skipped records with --accept-gaps, which records kc.offsets_not_migrated in acceptedGaps.

notes.reason: The input holds at least one secret as a literal value. migrate wrote a variable reference instead, but the input file itself contains the secret.
notes.fix: Fill the variables in secrets.env.template from your secret store, and replace the literal in the Kafka Connect config with a config-provider reference.

notes.reason: refresh.topics.enabled is absent (true), so MirrorMaker discovers new topics; the pipeline reads a fixed topic list.
sync.topic.configs.enabled is absent (true), so MirrorMaker syncs topic configs to the destination; the pipeline does not.
notes.fix: Create the destination topics ahead of time with the source topics' configs, or set sync.topic.configs.enabled=false if they already match.

notes.reason: sync.topic.acls.enabled is absent (true), so MirrorMaker syncs topic ACLs to the destination; the pipeline does not.
notes.fix: Set the ACLs on the destination topics ahead of time, or set sync.topic.acls.enabled=false.

notes.reason: replication.factor is absent, so MirrorMaker creates remote topics with replication factor 2; Conduit's Kafka destination creates topics with the broker's defaults.
emit.offset-syncs.enabled is absent (true), so MirrorMaker writes offset syncs for checkpointing; the pipeline does not, and consumer offsets cannot be translated for this flow.
heartbeats.replication.enabled is absent (true), so MirrorMaker replicates heartbeat topics; the pipeline reads only the listed topics.

Kafka Connect does not retry a failed operation by default (errors.retry.timeout=0). Conduit restarts a failed pipeline through pipeline recovery, so a transient failure that stopped the connector may not stop the pipeline.
Kafka Connect's default header converter types header values; Conduit carries headers as metadata strings.
